newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 13.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- Fourteen members of two North Korean families defect to South Korea aboard a boat in the Yellow Sea, the Defence Ministry said.

- South Korea's LG Chemical says it has signed a contract with Smithkline Beecham Plc to export antibiotic manufacturing technology at $37.5 million. The British company will also pay 30 billion won annually to LG Chemical over the next 20 years.
- The South Korean Red Cross plans to deliver 3,600 tonnes of corn to North Korea next week.

- Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha expresses confidence that North Korea will join proposed four-way peace talks by this summer to avert famine. The talks involve the two Koreas, the United States and China.
- Hyundai Electronics announces it has developed a 1 gigabyte synchronous dynamic random access momory chip using the new "silicon-on-insulator" technology.
- Deputy Prime Minister and Finance and Economy Minister Kang Kyong-shik reaffirms that South Korea will support North Korea's entry into the Asian Development Bank.
- Lee Hoi-Chang, chairman of the ruling New Korea Party, spurns opposition demands that his party reveals all facts about funds used in the 1992 presidential election campaign.
